# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91 (Bu-Vb Pc91)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vassikasāṭikā-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91) is a Vinaya rule establishing that a monk who makes a rainy-season robe (*vassikasāṭikā*) exceeding the permitted standard measurements must cut it down to size and confess an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship, Valentina Stache-Rosen highlights that while rules 89 and 90 of the *Upāliparipṛcchāsūtra* treat upper and lower robes, Pācittiya 91 in the Pali tradition specifically concerns the rainy-season robe [Stache-Rosen 1984]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule applies exclusively to monks, pointing to a discrepancy in the commentary *Samantapāsādikā* regarding the classification of rainy-season robe regulations as inapplicable to nuns while simultaneously discussing monastic boundary determinations (*sīmā*) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule is shared across the Vinaya literature of diverse early Buddhist schools. Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include the Pali *Bhikkhupātimokkha* (Pc 91) and *Parivāra*, as well as Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Dharmaguptaka Pātimokkha and Vibhaṅga texts preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan (where it is often numbered as Pācittiya 87, 88, or 89) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers substantial text reuse between this rule and surrounding Vibhaṅga size-restriction rules—principally Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 89, Pācittiya 90, Pācittiya 88, Pācittiya 87, and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22—as well as robe-related *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* rules and the *Parivāra* (Katāpattivāra) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus establishes automatic cross-language alignments with Tibetan Kanjur Vinaya sections and the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122), corresponding to Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya parallels [DharmaNexus].
